page: OVHcloud b2-60-flex is a general-purpose cloud instance configured with 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs based on the x86_64 Intel Haswell architecture running at 2.0 GHz without Hyper-Threading. The compute resources are paired with 60.0 GB of system memory, providing 3.75 GB per core. For local storage, the instance includes a bundled 50 GB SSD. Baseline network throughput is rated at 1 Gbps, and no hardware GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are provisioned.

Benchmark results demonstrate a clear split between single-threaded and parallel processing capacity. Single-core performance falls into the bottom 25%, with Geekbench single-core scoring 1084.0 and stress-ng single-core reaching 1064.88. In contrast, multi-threaded metrics reach average tier output across PassMark CPU (18823.44), Geekbench multi-core (7560.0), and stress-ng multi-core (15223.28). Memory throughput follows a similar pattern: cached reads reach 1350.63 GB/sec, while uncached write bandwidth settles at a lower-tier 21.28 GB/sec.

Hardware tradeoffs focus on architecture age and local disk sizing. The legacy Haswell core structure lacks AVX-512 extensions and higher base clock speeds, which limits single-threaded throughput and complex instruction processing such as 7B model text generation (6.9 tokens/sec). Additionally, the 50 GB local SSD serves strictly as a base boot or temporary volume rather than a large data repository.

In terms of qualitative efficiency, the b2-60-flex balances a large memory footprint with dedicated multi-core capacity. It delivers steady throughput for parallelized, non-bursting workloads. Best-fit applications include multi-threaded compilation, web serving, Redis caching nodes, background worker clusters, and general-purpose microservice architectures.
description: OVHcloud b2-60-flex is a general-purpose virtual machine equipped with 16 dedicated physical x86_64 cores running on an Intel Haswell architecture at 2.0 GHz. The platform features 60.0 GB of RAM, a 50 GB bundled SSD, and a 1 Gbps network baseline, operating without dedicated GPU hardware. Benchmark evaluations show below-average single-core CPU throughput alongside average multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics, such as a PassMark CPU score of 18823.44 and Geekbench multi-core score of 7560.0. The lack of modern instruction sets like AVX-512 and modest per-core clock rates limit intensive single-threaded computational tasks. However, the balance of 16 dedicated threads and 60 GB RAM provides consistent multi-threaded execution. This makes the instance suitable for distributed microservices, multi-threaded application compilation, Redis caching instances, and medium-scale web server fleets.
